events.text: Setup

Step 1 of 4: Setup

Here is how this works:

```
You give:  your resume, the job posting, a few sentences in your own words
   ↓
I write a draft, from your facts only
   ↓
A second AI, from a different company, checks it without knowing who wrote it
   ↓
Automatic checks, then you approve every changed line
   ↓
Your resume, the job requirements it does not show, and likely interview questions
```

It runs by itself; you answer a few questions along the way.

**What I read from your resume:**
- Biology Teacher, Public High School, August 2019 to Present
- Student Teacher, Public Middle School, January 2019 to May 2019
- Education: M.Ed. Curriculum and Instruction (2022), B.S. Biology (2018), Certificate in Instructional Design (2026)

If any of that is misread, tell me.

**One question:** the posting asks for a portfolio of work samples. Do you have a link to one (for example where your hand hygiene Rise course lives), or a LinkedIn profile you'd like on the resume? If not, that's fine; most recruiters do look for LinkedIn, though.

The posting doesn't state a level, so I'm assuming an entry to mid level Instructional Designer role in the United States (hybrid, Charlotte, NC). Correct me if that's off.

**My plan:**
- **Quick review:** I write the draft, and one second AI from another company checks it blind. The other AI I could add only offers a faster, lighter model than mine, so a full council (three AIs drafting and critiquing each other) wouldn't be a fair match here. It would also take longer and use several times as much of your AI plans. Solo (copies of me checking myself) is a weaker option.
- No role research (the posting already says what they want), I polish the final wording (or you can), and a plain-text copy while we work, with PDF or Word when it's final.

**Consent:**
I've hidden your name and contact details. They come back at the end.

The second AI is OpenAI's Codex, running the model gpt-6-astra. Your working files are in the `.tribunal` folder inside ..

This text, including your employers, job history and the pages your links point to, will go to Codex under its terms and your account settings there. Some keep their own history, and the text can still identify you. Leave out anything confidential to an employer, and check whether this employer allows AI help with applications.

Answer the question above, or say "yes" to take the defaults and go ahead.
Quick review, please. Yes to the defaults, go ahead. No other links.

Step 3 of 4: Review and sign-off

The second AI's review is back. As a hiring manager it said it would not phone you yet, for one reason: the posting requires Storyline and you've only watched demos. Nothing in the resume can honestly fix that, so I've left it as a gap you should know about. It read the resume as an entry-level instructional designer with a lot of teaching experience.

**What I changed without asking (wording only, no facts changed):**
- The summary now says you built one portfolio course in Rise, so it doesn't sound like you build Rise courses regularly.
- "Had a nurse check the content" is now "Asked a nurse friend to check the content", your own words.
- "Raised the AP Biology pass rate" is now "pass rate went from 58% in 2022 to 71% in 2025", right above the line on your weekly practice quizzes, so the reader sees both without the resume claiming one caused the other.
- Moved the lab safety training for about 40 teachers up, since it's your clearest example of teaching adults.
- Took "classroom management" out of the skills; it matters less for this job.
- I kept the Science Olympiad line and your video lessons as two short lines; the page has plenty of room (about 300 words).

The working resume is at .tribunal/resume.md.

**Questions about facts:**
1. Your old resume says "Articulate Rise". I wrote "Articulate Rise 360", the name the posting uses. Is the Rise you used Rise 360 (the web version inside Articulate 360)?
2. Did your nurse friend actually check the module, and did you change anything because of what she said? If so, one sentence on what changed would help.
3. For the 2023 lab safety training: did you design the workshop yourself (objectives, materials, activities), deliver one someone else wrote, or both?
4. These skills come only from your old resume: lesson planning, differentiated instruction, Google Workspace. Are they still current, and true as written?
5. Only if true, since the posting asks for them and the resume doesn't show them yet: have you ever done any of these?
   - published or maintained courses in Cornerstone, or any LMS besides Canvas
   - accessibility work, such as captions on your videos, alt text, or checking against WCAG
   - job aids (quick reference sheets, checklists)
   - measured whether a training worked, beyond grades (feedback forms, surveys, a follow-up check)

Are all of these true, and could you explain each in an interview? Tell me any to fix. If you don't know a number, I'll leave it out, so please don't estimate.

Please answer the questions above, by number is fine.

1. Yes, it's Rise 360, the same tool.
2. Yes, she reviewed the hand hygiene module content for accuracy. You could call her a subject matter expert for that one module. I don't remember changing anything specific.
3. I put it together myself from the district's safety rules and ran it, in person, in August 2023. No formal feedback.
4. Lesson planning and Google Workspace, yes, every week. Leave differentiated instruction off.
5. No Cornerstone, only Canvas. I add captions to all my Camtasia videos and alt text in Canvas, but I don't know WCAG formally. No job aids. I've never measured a training beyond grades.

Step 4 of 4: Finalise

Thanks, all of that is in. What changed from your answers:
- The nurse line now says she reviewed the content for accuracy as subject matter expert for the module.
- The lab safety training is now two lines: you put it together from the district's safety rules, and ran it in person in August 2023 for about 40 teachers. I added no feedback or results, since there were none.
- New line: you add captions to all your Camtasia videos and alt text in Canvas. I didn't write "WCAG", since you don't know it formally.
- Differentiated instruction is off; lesson planning moved into the instructional design skills.
- Cornerstone, job aids and measuring training stay off the resume.

The automatic check now finds nothing to fix. The resume is about 330 words, well within one page.

Your resume, with your name and contact details back in, is at .tribunal/final.md.

Two things before we finish:
- I can send it to the second AI for one more blind look at the final version. It takes a few minutes and is optional.
- For the file, you'll get it as a plain-text copy (Markdown) that you can paste into Word or Google Docs. Making a PDF here would need an extra tool installed first.

Is it final? Say "it's final", or tell me what to change, and whether you'd like that one more look.
No thanks. Yes, it's final. Markdown is fine.
final check: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 329 words

Step 4 of 4: Finalise

Your resume is done: .tribunal/final.md. The last automatic check found nothing to fix. To send it, paste it into Word or Google Docs, apply heading styles, and save it as a PDF or Word file.

**What this job asks for that the resume does not show:**
- Articulate Storyline 360. It's a required qualification, and the hiring manager review named it as the reason it wouldn't phone yet. Even a small practice project in a free trial would give you something true to list.
- A portfolio link. The posting asks for work samples; if you can put the hand hygiene module online, add the link next to the project.
- Cornerstone, or any LMS besides Canvas.
- Accessibility to WCAG 2.1 AA. The resume shows your captions and alt text, but not the standard itself.
- Measuring training effectiveness. You learned the Kirkpatrick model, but haven't used it on a training yet.
- Job aids.
- Working with subject matter experts at work. The resume shows one nurse reviewing one module.
- A healthcare background. Your biology background counts as science, which the posting also names.

**Questions your resume will invite in an interview:**
- "What did you build in the hand hygiene course yourself, and what did the nurse check?" This tests how much of the course was yours and how you work with an expert.
- "How were the 58% and 71% pass rates counted, and what else changed between those years?" This tests whether you can talk about a result honestly, without claiming the weekly practice caused all of it.
- "How did you turn the district's safety rules into a two-hour workshop?" This tests your design decisions for adult learners.
- "In the cells unit rewrite, which part was yours, and how did the three of you match lessons to objectives and quiz items?" This tests collaboration and how you line up objectives with assessment.
- "How would you use ADDIE or Kirkpatrick on a real project?" This tests whether you can turn what you learned in the certificate into practice.

The working files are in the .tribunal folder, and I'll keep them unless you'd like them deleted.

Save what you told me (your resume, your own words and the facts you confirmed) on this computer, so your next job needs fewer questions? It stays in ~/.resume-tribunal/, goes nowhere else, and you can delete the folder any time.
No thanks.
